locations.name: A plaza where mariachi are warming up
A lucha libre gym down a side street
A rooftop terraza overlooking the Zócalo
A sprawling mercado selling everything at once
A courtyard mid-mural, paint still wet

collaborator.gift: a cascabel anklet, still warm from her ankle

preShowChoices.label: Play it exactly as rehearsed
preShowChoices.description: Every cue where it should be. No surprises tonight.

preShowChoices.label: Open the floor for the crowd to answer
preShowChoices.description: Let the room talk back for once.

preShowChoices.label: Bring Ximena up to trade rhythms
preShowChoices.description: Hand her half the song, no rehearsal at all.

minigames.title: Interview
minigames.introText: A local zine caught wind of the show and wants five minutes before soundcheck.
minigames.outroText: "Great stuff," the writer says, already typing. "This'll run before the weekend."
minigames.outroTextRough: The writer nods, polite but unconvinced. "I'll see what I can do with this."

minigames.title: Radio Call-In
minigames.introText: Ximena's borrowed the community radio's mic for a two-question segment. "Keep it short," she grins.
minigames.outroText: "That's a wrap," Ximena laughs, already coiling the mic cable. "You're a natural."
minigames.outroTextRough: "A little stiff," Ximena teases, "but nobody's checking."

questions.prompt: "What's the tour taught you so far?"

mex_arrival.speaker: narrator
mex_arrival.text: The bus climbs out of a haze of smog into afternoon gold, volcano-shadowed and loud with a hundred radios playing a hundred different songs at once. Someone's already selling roasted corn and paletas at the edge of the lot.

choices.label: Take in the skyline
Get the gear off the bus
Check on Jun, already recording street sounds

mex_arrival_view.speaker: narrator
mex_arrival_view.text: Ash-grey volcano on the horizon, cathedral bells layered under six lanes of traffic. The city doesn't quiet down for anyone passing through, and somehow that's exactly the relief you needed.

mex_arrival_gear.speaker: narrator
mex_arrival_gear.text: The amp case squeals on one wheel now, louder with every city you drag it through. Someone will fix that eventually — probably not today, probably not this whole tour.

mex_arrival_jun.speaker: jun
mex_arrival_jun.text: "Listen to this," Jun says, phone held out toward a sound truck blasting cumbia through one busted, overdriven speaker. "That distortion right there — that's the whole song, honestly."

mex_loc_taqueria.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria.text: Onions hit hot metal and the whole block turns to look before going back to its business. The woman running the grill has clearly done this ten thousand times before today, without once looking bored.

choices.label: Order one of everything on the menu
Watch her work the grill in silence
Ask what makes hers different

mex_loc_taqueria_order.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria_order.text: Five tacos in, someone at the table finally admits defeat and pushes their plate away. It wasn't you, and you're quietly, unreasonably proud of that fact.

mex_loc_taqueria_order_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria_order_after.text: The pride lasts until the van, where it becomes a stomachache, which somehow does not diminish it at all.

mex_loc_taqueria_watch.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria_watch.text: No wasted motion anywhere — hands, tongs, the flick of salsa, the exact half-turn of the wrist. You could set a metronome to the rhythm of her hands and never once lose the beat.

mex_loc_taqueria_watch_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria_watch_after.text: You mention it to Theo, who nods slowly and says “that’s the gig” — meaning hers, meaning also yours.

mex_loc_taqueria_ask.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria_ask.text: "Thirty years of practice," she says, not even glancing up from the grill. "Also, don't tell anyone, but it's the onions." She winks like it's a secret worth actually keeping.

mex_loc_taqueria_ask_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_taqueria_ask_after.text: You do tell someone. Immediately. It is the first thing out of your mouth back at the van.

mex_loc_plaza.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza.text: Trumpets tune against each other in a loose, happy argument that somehow resolves itself every few bars. A mariachi in silver braid winks at you and keeps right on playing, unbothered by the audience.

choices.label: Tip them for a song
Ask to learn a riff
Sit on the curb and just listen

mex_loc_plaza_tip.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza_tip.text: They play the whole song again, just for you this time, a little louder and considerably showier than before. Worth every peso, and then some.

mex_loc_plaza_tip_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza_tip_after.text: They wave the second time you pass. Being recognised in a city you leave tomorrow is its own small ache.

mex_loc_plaza_learn.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza_learn.text: Your fingers won't cooperate no matter how slowly he plays it. The trumpeter laughs, not unkindly, and shows you the fingering one more patient time.

mex_loc_plaza_learn_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza_learn_after.text: You get it wrong all the way home and keep trying anyway, badly, on the edge of the van seat.

mex_loc_plaza_listen.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza_listen.text: Nobody asks you to move along. You stay long enough to learn the shape of the song without ever meaning to memorize a single note of it.

mex_loc_plaza_listen_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_plaza_listen_after.text: You hum it wrong at soundcheck. Jun corrects you. Neither of you knows the name of it.

mex_loc_lucha.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha.text: A masked luchador vaults clean over the ropes as the crowd roars in one throat, like a single enormous animal waking up. Someone presses a foam finger shaped like a fist into your hand.

choices.label: Cheer until your throat gives out
Study how the crowd moves as one
Buy a cheap replica mask at the door

mex_loc_lucha_cheer.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha_cheer.text: You lose your voice a full day before soundcheck, hoarse and grinning anyway, throat raw for the rest of the week. Worth it, probably — you'll find out for certain tomorrow.

mex_loc_lucha_cheer_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha_cheer_after.text: You sing anyway that night. It costs you the top of your range and you do not regret one note.

mex_loc_lucha_study.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha_study.text: Two thousand strangers, breathing on exactly the same beat without ever once being asked to or rehearsing it. You want that sound onstage tonight, whatever it costs you.

mex_loc_lucha_study_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha_study_after.text: You do not get that sound tonight. You get about a third of it, which is more than you had yesterday.

mex_loc_lucha_mask.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha_mask.text: The mask smells like plastic and somebody else's cologne. You wear it for the rest of the walk home anyway, unreasonably pleased with the whole purchase.

mex_loc_lucha_mask_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_lucha_mask_after.text: It hangs from the van’s rearview for the rest of the tour, swaying through three more cities.

mex_loc_terraza.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza.text: The Zócalo spreads out below, flag snapping hard in the wind, cathedral lit gold against a bruised purple sky. Thunderheads are already stacking up fast over the hills to the west.

choices.label: Stay and watch the storm roll in
Head inside before it breaks
Call home before the signal drops

mex_loc_terraza_storm.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza_storm.text: Lightning finds the cathedral spire twice in under a minute. You count the seconds after each strike, out of an old childhood habit you never quite dropped.

mex_loc_terraza_storm_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza_storm_after.text: Four seconds. Then three. Then the rain arrives and settles the argument about whether to run.

mex_loc_terraza_in.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza_in.text: You make it inside one drop ahead of the downpour. Below, the entire street breaks into a run for cover, laughing, all at once.

mex_loc_terraza_in_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza_in_after.text: You watch from the doorway, dry, slightly guilty, entirely delighted. The street empties in under a minute.

mex_loc_terraza_call.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza_call.text: The call drops twice before it finally connects. "We're fine," you say, over a crack of thunder. "Better than fine, actually. Really good, even."

mex_loc_terraza_call_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_terraza_call_after.text: You mean it when you say it. That is the part that surprises you afterwards.

mex_loc_mercado.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mercado.text: Vendors call out prices over each other in a rhythm the block took generations to perfect and never once wrote down. Rowan is already three stalls deep, completely and happily gone.

choices.label: Haggle over a hand drum
Go find Rowan
Get pleasantly, deliberately lost

mex_loc_mercado_haggle.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mercado_haggle.text: You get it for half price and a promise to come back tomorrow with the whole band in tow. You will not, in fact, come back tomorrow.

mex_loc_mercado_haggle_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mercado_haggle_after.text: You think about it again three cities later and feel briefly, genuinely bad about the promise.

mex_loc_mercado_rowan.speaker: rowan
mex_loc_mercado_rowan.text: "Every single stall has a different beat," Rowan says, delighted, tapping along on an overturned bucket someone's using as a stool, completely lost to it.

mex_loc_mercado_rowan_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mercado_rowan_after.text: They keep the rhythm all the way to the van. It turns up in the second song that night, quietly.

mex_loc_mercado_lost.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mercado_lost.text: You take four wrong turns on purpose and find a courtyard nobody mentioned in any guidebook you've ever read, on any tour, in any city.

mex_loc_mercado_lost_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mercado_lost_after.text: You could not find it again if you tried. You do try, an hour later, and you cannot.

mex_loc_mural.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mural.text: A muralist balances on a paint-flecked ladder, finishing a wall of birds mid-flight. Half the courtyard has stopped just to watch her work.

choices.label: Ask what the mural means
Steady the ladder for her

mex_loc_mural_ask.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mural_ask.text: "Everyone who left and came back," she says, not looking down. "There's more of us than you'd think."

mex_loc_mural_ask_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mural_ask_after.text: You look for longer than you meant to. Mira waits without saying anything about it.

mex_loc_mural_help.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mural_help.text: She finishes a wing in half the time, unbothered, like the extra hand was expected all along.

mex_loc_mural_help_after.speaker: narrator
mex_loc_mural_help_after.text: Your line is the crooked one, third from the left. She leaves it exactly as you painted it.

mex_rel_mira.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira.text: "Nobody here knows who we are, and they're dancing anyway," Mira says, delighted, almost disbelieving. "I don't think I knew how much I needed exactly that."

choices.label: Then let's stay unknown a little longer
They'll know soon. Enjoy it while it lasts.

mex_rel_mira_a.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira_a.text: "Deal," she says, and clearly means it — for once not performing a single thing for anybody, including herself, including you.

mex_rel_mira_b.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira_b.text: Her smile flickers, just slightly, before she catches it and buries it back in the noise of the street, out of long habit.

mex_rel_theo.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo.text: "Even the city has a backbeat here," Theo says, wiping sweat off his neck, "and it never once stops long enough to actually breathe."

choices.label: Find shade and sit with him a while
Then match it. Don't fight the pace.

mex_rel_theo_a.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo_a.text: The shade helps. So does not talking for a while. Theo's shoulders finally, visibly drop for the first time all week, maybe all tour.

mex_rel_theo_b.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo_b.text: He tries it, hesitant at first, then less so. Something in his playing loosens that hasn't loosened in weeks of tour, maybe longer than that.

mex_rel_jun.speaker: jun
mex_rel_jun.text: "I want to mic literally everything in this city," Jun says, already unspooling cable across the sidewalk. "The buses, the vendors, the church bells. All of it, layered."

choices.label: Help them chase every sound on the block
Pick one sound and commit to it

mex_rel_jun_a.speaker: jun
mex_rel_jun_a.text: Two hours later you have forty minutes of horns, bells, and one deeply confused stray dog barking directly into the microphone at close range.

mex_rel_jun_b.speaker: jun
mex_rel_jun_b.text: Jun picks the cathedral bells, reluctantly, already mourning every single sound they didn't get the chance to record, notebook full of what-ifs.

mex_rel_rowan.speaker: rowan
mex_rel_rowan.text: "Ximena asked ME to sit in on percussion tonight," Rowan says, stunned, saying it twice like it won't stick otherwise. "Not the band. Me, specifically."

choices.label: Then go. This is your moment.
Be nervous about it together first

mex_rel_rowan_a.speaker: rowan
mex_rel_rowan_a.text: Rowan's already gone, jogging back toward the plaza before you've even finished the sentence out loud, bass case still half-open and forgotten by the curb.

mex_rel_rowan_b.speaker: rowan
mex_rel_rowan_b.text: "Okay," Rowan says, steadier now, squaring their shoulders like it helps. "Okay. I can actually do this. I think I can actually do this."

mex_rel_rowan2.speaker: rowan
mex_rel_rowan2.text: Rowan comes back from the lesson with Ximena buzzing, hands still moving through a pattern they won't quite stop repeating. "She said I have good hands," Rowan says. "Good hands."

choices.label: Ask them to show you the pattern
Let them have this one, unshared

mex_rel_rowan2_a.speaker: rowan
mex_rel_rowan2_a.text: Rowan teaches you three bars badly and patiently, correcting your hands twice, clearly enjoying being the one who knows something for once, for a change.

mex_rel_rowan2_b.speaker: rowan
mex_rel_rowan2_b.text: Rowan just nods, grateful, and keeps tapping the pattern out quietly for the rest of the walk back to the bus, not needing an audience for it.

mex_rel_theo_letter.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo_letter.text: A message finally loads through spotty signal. "My sister's checking in again," Theo says. "She's the one who noticed, before I did, that I wasn't okay last year."

choices.label: Tell her the truth — you're actually doing okay
Not yet. Some things need more time to be true.

mex_rel_theo_letter_a.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo_letter_a.text: He sends it before he can second-guess it. Three words back, almost instantly: "Good. Stay there."

mex_rel_theo_letter_b.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo_letter_b.text: He types four different replies and deletes all of them. "Later," he says out loud, to nobody.

mex_rel_theo_letter_fallback.speaker: theo
mex_rel_theo_letter_fallback.text: Theo's phone buzzes. He glances at it, pockets it without reading further, and says nothing about it.

mex_rel_mira_why.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira_why.text: "A producer once told me I'd never carry a room without a bigger voice," Mira says. "I think about that every single time we walk on stage."

choices.label: He was wrong. You carry every room.
Maybe it's time to let his voice go

mex_rel_mira_why_a.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira_why_a.text: "Say that again after tonight's set," she says, half-joking, half not joking at all.

mex_rel_mira_why_b.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira_why_b.text: She's quiet a moment. "Working on it," she says. "Slower than I'd like. But working on it."

mex_rel_mira_why_fallback.speaker: mira
mex_rel_mira_why_fallback.text: Mira starts to mention a producer from years back, then catches herself and asks about the set list instead.

mex_preshow.speaker: narrator
mex_preshow.text: Ximena's already warming up just outside, cascabels jingling softly against the doorframe with every shift of her weight. The whole block seems to be finding its way toward the venue tonight, unhurried.

mex_aftershow.speaker: narrator
mex_aftershow.text: The last drumbeat doesn't really end so much as get absorbed straight into the street outside, which is still going, and shows absolutely no sign of stopping any time soon.

choices.label: Follow the rhythm out into the street
Stay and help Ximena pack up

mex_aftershow_drum.speaker: narrator
mex_aftershow_drum.text: You bring the hand drum out into the street after the show, and a stranger starts a rhythm on it that has nothing to do with tonight's set list at all — and somehow it still fits.

choices.label: Follow the rhythm out into the street
Stay and help Ximena pack up

mex_aftershow_a.speaker: narrator
mex_aftershow_a.text: You end up three blocks away, still playing, strangers keeping time on car hoods and folding chairs and each other's shoulders, nobody counting the beat out loud.

mex_aftershow_b.speaker: narrator
mex_aftershow_b.text: Ximena presses the anklet into your hands before you can even think to argue about it. "For the road," she says simply, like that settles it.

mex_journal.speaker: narrator
mex_journal.text: You write: somewhere a community radio host still has our two-question segment saved, Ximena's idea. Mexico City never once stopped moving, and somehow that was the most restful place we've played.

mex_journal_generic.speaker: narrator
mex_journal_generic.text: You write: Mexico City never once stopped moving, not for a single second, and somehow that was the most restful place we've played all tour.
